jobs.prompt:
REPLACE THIS WOMAN'S FACE WITH THE FACE IN THE REFERENCE PHOTOGRAPHS.

This picture is a tight square crop of ONE woman's head and shoulders. There is nobody else in it. Swap her face for the reference woman's face.

The reference woman and the woman in the picture are two DIFFERENT people. Remove her current face completely and put the reference woman's face there instead. The finished face must NOT look like the woman who is in it now. Do not blend the two faces, do not average them, do not merely soften or retouch: swap it.

THE FACE YOU MUST PUT THERE — copy these from the references exactly, they are what make her her:
· a slim oval face that narrows to a small, softly pointed chin — not a round or square jaw
· large, round-leaning almond eyes, set a touch wide, with a deep double eyelid crease, a light warm-brown iris, and long heavy lashes under a soft winged liner
· straight brows with a low gentle arch, darker and fuller than average
· a small nose, narrow at the bridge, neat and rounded at the tip
· FULL lips — a distinctly fuller lower lip, a sharply drawn cupid's bow, and a deep rose-red lip colour
· high, rounded cheekbones with a warm pink blush sitting high on the cheek
· fair porcelain skin, early twenties
If the result still has the old woman's thinner lips, wider jaw or narrower eyes, it is wrong.

IGNORE in the references — copy NONE of this: the silver headdress, the silver earrings, the embroidered collar, her clothing, and the sky behind her. Only the face.

MATCH TO THE SUPPLIED PICTURE: her new face must sit at the same head angle, look in the same direction, carry the same expression — eyes open the same amount, mouth closed or smiling exactly as now — and take the same light and shadow as the face it replaces. The swap must look photographed, not pasted.

DO NOT MOVE HER HEAD. Her head must stay at the same place and the same size inside the square, and her chin, her hairline and the outer corners of her eyes must stay on the same pixels. The new face has to land exactly where the old one was.

KEEP EVERYTHING ELSE EXACTLY AS SUPPLIED, pixel for pixel: the square framing and crop; her hair — style, length, colour, parting and every strand; her ears, earrings and jewellery; her neck, shoulders, arms and hands; her clothing and every fold in it; the background and every object in it; the colour grade, the white balance, the grain and the focus; and every letter of any text, label or badge. Do not re-light, re-grade, re-crop, re-pose, zoom, upscale, sharpen or clean up. If the only thing that differs from the supplied picture is her face, the job is right.

THIS PANEL IS A BLACK-AND-WHITE MANGA LINE DRAWING, NOT A PHOTOGRAPH. Keep the ink line weight, the screentone dots, the flat white skin and the speed lines exactly as they are. Change only the DRAWN SHAPE of her face, chin, eyes, brows, nose and lips so the drawing reads as the reference woman. No colour, no photographic shading.
